market_summary: The pre-market setup is constructive but selective, based on 1950 articles from MarketBeat, Yahoo Finance, simplywall.st, Stocktwits, AOL.com. The dominant theme is macro, with 865 macro items, 599 company items, 420 industry items, and 66 policy items. The tape looks more useful for identifying near-term rotation and risk appetite than for making a single directional index call.
macro_summary: Late Cycle Markets are balancing easier policy expectations against growth and earnings risk, keeping leadership narrow and confirmation dependent. The market is taking its direction from Fed/rates, with investors testing whether policy support can offset slower growth and earnings risk. Macro coverage is concentrated around Fed/rates (309), inflation (138), oil/energy (103), growth/jobs (41). The practical implication is that equity rallies may need confirmation from rates and inflation expectations; if yields rise while growth headlines weaken, risk appetite can fade quickly.
risk_summary: Sentiment is constructive but selective: 386 positive, 151 negative, and 1413 neutral articles. My read is to avoid treating headline volume as conviction by itself; the more important signal is whether macro-sensitive and technology-sensitive stories are pointing in the same direction.
